settings.html:
What the evidence shows, in short

  • Nearly 1 in 2 were graded clearly smoother after 4 weeks — 22 of 45 people, against none on placebo (controlled trial, 10% Argireline)
  • Wrinkle depth down up to 30% in 30 days (the developers' own small study — indicative only)
  • Forehead roughness fell while placebo rose (second controlled trial, day 20)
  • No side effects were reported in any of the controlled trials (45 people, 4 weeks, around the eyes)
  • The one independent imaging test found no difference — it is in the table below rather than left out

Argireline Evidence & Sources

Every study this page relies on, with its published title, our reading of it and a link to the source. Graded A controlled human trial measured by instrument · B smaller, uncontrolled or manufacturer data · C tests on skin samples · Review a summary of other work.

StudyGradeWhat it found, and what it does not show

The anti-wrinkle efficacy of a synthetic hexapeptide in Chinese subjects: a randomized, placebo-controlled study

Wang et al., 2013 · Am J Clin Dermatol · 14:147–53

PubMed →		A60 adults (45 active, 15 placebo), 10% Argireline twice daily around the eyes for 4 weeks, double-blind and placebo-controlled. 22 of 45 (48.9%) were graded clearly improved against 0 of 15 on placebo — a count of people, not a wrinkle measurement. Silicone replicas showed roughness down (p < 0.01). Product supplied by the Argireline marketer in China.

The efficacy study of the combination of tripeptide-10-citrulline and acetyl hexapeptide-3

Raikou et al., 2017 · J Cosmet Dermatol · 16:271–8

PubMed →		A24 women, about 6 per arm, 10% Argireline twice daily for 60 days. Forehead roughness −7.4% at day 20 against +4.3% on placebo (P = .022); the day-60 difference was not significant. Skin held moisture better at days 20 and 40. Very small; actives supplied by the maker's distributor.

Acetyl hexapeptide-3 in a cosmetic formulation acts on skin mechanical properties

Tadini et al., 2015 · Braz J Pharm Sci · 51(4)

no PubMed record		A40 women, 10% Argireline for 2 and 4 weeks against the vehicle. Skin became more uniform in how it resists stretching (p < 0.05). Elasticity did not change, and hydration rose with every formulation including the vehicle — so it does not support a hydration claim.

Investigating the effects of Argireline in a skin serum containing hyaluronic acids on skin surface wrinkles

Henseler, 2023 · GMS Interdiscip Plast Reconstr Surg

PubMed →		A — negativeThe only independent objective-imaging test, and it found nothing. 19 women, split-face, the same serum with and without Argireline for 4 weeks. No significant difference (wrinkles p = 0.829). Concentration not stated. Reported here because leaving it out would misrepresent the evidence.

A synthetic hexapeptide with antiwrinkle activity

Blanes-Mira et al., 2002 · Int J Cosmet Sci · 24:303–10

PubMed →		BThe developers' own study. An emulsion with 10% Argireline reduced measured wrinkle depth up to 30% in 30 days. Small, and the full text is paywalled and has not been read by us, so the number of participants and the vehicle result stay unverified. Always quote it as “up to”.

Manufacturer in-vivo study, reported in trade press (not peer-reviewed)

Lipotec, 2013 · Personal Care Magazine

no PubMed record		B24 women, split-face, a cream with 2% Argireline solution twice daily for 7 days. Wrinkle volume −20.6% and length −15.9%. The ingredient maker's own unpublished study, at a fifth of our concentration, and it is not stated whether the figure is against baseline or against the placebo side.

Anti-Wrinkle Efficacy of a Microneedle Patch with Acetyl Hexapeptide-8 and EGF

An et al., 2019 · Ann Dermatol

PubMed →		A — other deliveryA dissolving microneedle patch, not a serum. 52 women, once weekly for 29 days: fine periorbital wrinkles −14.6% against −5.9% for the patch alone. Listed for completeness; a needle that delivers peptide through the skin surface cannot stand in for a leave-on serum.

In vitro skin penetration of acetyl hexapeptide-8 from a cosmetic formulation

Hoppel et al., 2015 · Eur J Pharm Sci

PubMed →		CFranz cells on pig-ear skin. Water-rich emulsions delivered clearly more peptide than oil-rich ones. Formulation science, not an efficacy result: it says how a vehicle behaves, not what it does to a face.

Acetyl Hexapeptide-8 in Cosmeceuticals — A Review of Skin Permeability and Efficacy

Zdrada-Nowak et al., 2025 · Int J Mol Sci

PubMed →		ReviewConcludes that low penetration limits how much peptide is available and that reaching the neuromuscular junction “remains uncertain”, so any effect is likely to be in the upper skin. Misquotes Wang 2013 as a “49% reduction in wrinkle depth”; we cite Wang directly instead.

Published titles are quoted exactly as they appear in the journal. Where a study measured something we cannot claim for a leave-on serum — an injection, a microneedle patch, or a different concentration — it is listed and labelled rather than left out.
